_help: YOUR OWN RULES. They are checked before the built-in rules in tidyup.rules.json, which you never need to edit.
Same id as a built-in rule = replaces it. "disabled": true = switched off (the examples below are off until you remove that line).
After editing: python tidyup.py --check-rules   (validates)   and   python tidyup.py --explain "C:\some\path"   (shows which rule matches).
Paths are globs with '/' separators: * = inside one folder, ** = any depth, {a,b} = alternatives. Case does not matter.
action: safe | likely | review | info.  dir_rules mode: whole (folder as one item) | children (each entry inside, filtered by min_age_days).
file_rules: match by exts and/or names (file-name globs), optional path glob, min_age_days, min_size_kb, age_basis used|modified.
Optional on folder rules: exclude (globs), ps (PowerShell command used instead of deleting), system: true (may match inside C:\Windows etc.).

dir_rules.label: Build output in C:\git projects
dir_rules.how: Delete, or 'git clean -xdf' in the repo.

dir_rules.label: Old Teams meeting recordings
dir_rules.reason: Recordings are also stored in OneDrive/Stream.
dir_rules.how: Delete the local copies you no longer need.

file_rules.label: Old D365 deployable packages
file_rules.reason: Downloaded deployable packages are kept in LCS / Azure DevOps artifacts.
file_rules.how: Delete local copies of packages that are already deployed.

categories._note: Optional: add or move file extensions to a category, e.g. "D365 packages": [".axpp"]

compression_ratios._note: Optional: estimated saving (0-1) for extra compressible extensions, e.g. ".trx": 0.8
